references.text: Joshua warns Israel that the Lord will no longer drive out the nations before them if they break the covenant, which is directly linked to God's judgment in Judges 2:21.
Moses warns that if Israel does not drive out the inhabitants of the land, they will become thorns in their eyes. This is the background for God's decision not to drive out the nations.
God originally promised to drive out the nations little by little, but Israel's disobedience caused this process to be halted.
The angel of the Lord announces that God will not drive out the nations and that they will become a snare for Israel. This is the direct consequence of the verse.
Explains that the Lord allowed these nations to remain and did not drive them out quickly, which elaborates on God's decision in verse 21.
Describes which nations the Lord left behind to test Israel, as a direct follow-up to God's decision in chapter 2.
Tells of Joshua's death and that Israel served the Lord as long as the elders lived. This provides context for 'the nations that Joshua left when he died'.
